title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Account Note: Holding Several Jobs
content:
> A customer may hold any number of fire and smoke jobs at once, one for each separate loss; each job has its own tier, authorization, ledger and invoice.

This note applies to every Fire & Smoke Mitigation customer, from a homeowner with a single kitchen fire to a property manager or commercial owner with losses at several buildings.

## What the rule fixes

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Number of fire and smoke jobs one customer may hold at once | No maximum is set: any number |
| What each job corresponds to | One separate loss |
| Tier | Each job has its own |
| Cleaning authorization | Each job has its own |
| Ledger of charges and payments | Each job has its own |
| Invoice | Each job has its own |

## Points of judgement

- Holding one open Fire & Smoke Mitigation job places no ceiling on the customer holding another job for a separate loss; the company sets no maximum number of jobs per customer.
- Because each job carries its own tier, two jobs of the same customer can sit at different tiers; the tier of one job says nothing about the tier of the other.
- Because each job carries its own authorization, ledger and invoice, a signature, a charge or an invoice belongs to one job only.

## Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical property manager has a Fire & Smoke Mitigation job at Light Smoke and Soot Cleanup for a smoke loss in one building and a second job at Heavy Fire Cleanup for a separate fire in another building. The two jobs are two holdings: each was authorized on its own, each keeps its own ledger, and each receives its own invoice.
